newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee stable, London seen edging up.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee stable, London seen edging up.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were mostly stable on Tuesday, with supply staying ample amid the main crop harvest, traders said.

They said grade four Robusta was quoted at 3,200 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, unchanged from a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,400-$1,410 a tonne, also unchanged from last week.
The traders said they expected London's benchmark July contract to open higher by between $20-$40 later on Tuesday following gains in New York on Monday.
"Supply at the moment seems to be ample," one trader said. "But farmers are well informed of prices at the London terminal and prefer to hold back when prices there fall."
"They prefer to keep their beans when prices are lower because they know supply will get tight towards the end of the year because of a decline in production," he added.
Most traders said they expected supply to be squeezed from September, but one said it could come earlier.
"Bean arrival was only 600-700 tonnes in Lampung yesterday compared with 1,500 tonnes last Monday," the trader said. "Arrivals are usually at their peak on Mondays."
"It looks like it's going to be a tough year for the coffee business," he said.

Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters, said in early April the country's production was expected to fall by some 30 percent this year from an original forecast of 480,000 tonnes due to bad weather. He said the total exportable volume would amount to 220,000 tonnes.
One trader said they estimated that some 80,000 tonnes of the exportable volume had been committed.
